entities.name: Vakhtang VI of Kartli
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Vakhtang VI was a Georgian monarch (mepe) of the royal Bagrationi dynasty. He ruled the East Georgian Kingdom of Kartli as a vassal of Safavid Persia from 1716 to 1724. One of the most important and extraordinary statesman of early 18th-century Georgia, he is known as a notable legislator, scholar, critic, translator and poet. His reign was eventually terminated by the Ottoman invasion following the disintegration of Safavid Persia, which forced Vakhtang into exile in the Russian Empire. Vakhtang was unable to get the tsar's support for his kingdom and instead had to permanently stay with his northern neighbors for his own safety.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Vakhtang VI's reign as a vassal of Safavid Persia had significant regional impact on East Georgian Kingdom of Kartli, influencing its politics and culture. His efforts to modernize the kingdom were ultimately hindered by his inability to secure tsar's support from the Russian Empire.
